content.thinking: This looks like silent data corruption rather than a bad deployment—the system stopped updating month totals, so stored values are stale with no metrics alerting on it, which reconciliation would catch. I'll do a quick sanity check on logs but this is likely the right classification to go with.

hypotheses.subject: purchase_ledger.record_purchase month total (total_this_month_cents)
hypotheses.summary: Revision 26f1d7e deployed at 2026-10-11T16:24:00Z changed record_purchase so that total_this_month_cents is no longer updated. Every purchase recorded after that left the stored month total behind, so all 240 shopper totals are short. The service stayed fast and error-free, and the records already written stay wrong until they are rewritten.

supporting_evidence.claim: Alert: 240 of 240 shopper totals do not reconcile; oldest affected purchase recorded 2026-10-11T16:26:00Z; metrics flat across the whole window
Deploy 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2 at 2026-10-11T16:24:00Z removed the total_this_month_cents update from record_purchase ('The month is no longer carried')

hypotheses.subject: 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2
hypotheses.summary: The deployment shipped code that stopped maintaining the month total in the ledger. The fault is in the released code, and the symptom is incorrect stored totals.

supporting_evidence.claim: Deploy 26f1d7e removed the month-total addition from record_purchase, two minutes before the oldest affected purchase
